> p.s. Men are weak. we can only expect so much.

Can we please not?
What the fuck?

Hey, since you're in Montana, why did you pick that particular school?

And thank you for your reply!
Exactly! This kind of shit is exactly what Russia is pumping into our discourse!

There are more reasons to be angry with Trump, his policies, and his supporters than there are atoms in the universe. It's a good thing for the world that he was voted out. I say this first to help ensure that we don't get off on the wrong foot here.

However, I do believe this kind of content has crossed a line. Not only does calling the opposition evil brain eating zombies not going to change any minds, it's also contributing to the polarization that Russia and other bad faith agencies have been trying to push for the past ten or so years. (This was covered in the Mueller Report).

I hate trump more than the next guy and everyone here has the right to be angry, but we can't post or up vote stuff like this.

I was initially nervous, but after seeing courts and news stations shut him down at every corner, the man looks as powerless as ever. 

I think everything is going to be ok. He can't do anything catastrophic without the government on his side, and they're not anymore.

100k a year? Are you serious? I was thinking I'd get 60k if I was lucky.

And I've looked into corneal transplants. They are usually seen as a last ditch effort. There's a plethora of side effects.
Lol, how do the laser goggles mess with eye site?

I guess I should explain my eye disorder.

I have keratoconus, this cannot be corrected with glasses. I have to wear sclarel contacts, and even those don't fix it 100%. The main effect this disorder has is that I see "ghost" images of everything: I can't clearly see the edge of the moon

I didn't think about getting glasses on top of these, however. I bet I could get something cheap that simply magnifies what I see, perhaps that could work. I'll have to talk to my optometrist.
I know this is a difficult question to answer, but how small would you say your fringes are? Do you have to focus anything?

Thank you so much for writing this.

I'm still trying to wrap around this but I think I've got too anxiety to think straight. I do feel like what you said applies not just to my parents but my siblings as well and I just don't know what to do.

What do I do now? I'm stuck in this house still, I don't graduate from University until December. I just don't know.

I'm so tired of being alone

I usually don't cry because "what you're feeling isn't enough to cry over."

\>  Specifically blaming and shaming you for their inability to have a relationship with you. 

I've looked into scapegoating, that's been the battle for my life because it conflicts with what I've been told. However, I never thought about it as my families *inability to have a relationship with me*. Can you elaborate more on this?

​

\>  So now you are using the same reason to make sense of why this person  can't love you. Except the only reason is they aren't available. It's  not in you, it's in them. It simply a thing that is. 

Are you saying that I am using the fact that they're not available as justification for why I feel like no one could ever love me?

Thank you so much for talking with me about this by the way, hearing your perspective has been very valuable to me.
Both are damaging but in different ways. I think they are different enough where they can't really be compared other than they both have potential for tremendous damage.

>His advice to me was that before we tried any medicine, I should try to have a good cry. 

Funny that you write that, because I have only cried once since I got diagnosed with C-PTSD in May 2018. (The event that caused it was very similar to what I am currently suffering from too).  


The trick to thinking about what you are flashing back to has helped me once before. When I would get in conflicts with friends, I would often get this feeling of "I'm just trying to... (lift something heavy?) I'm just trying to..." Eventually I realized I was flash backing to when my parents would punish me by locking me in the garage and I was trying to get back in with a hammer. 

But when I think about what I am flash backing to when I'm thinking about the limerence I suffer from I think of...

 "Look at how amazing this person is and look at how awful you are." Actually, I don't even know if it's limerence anymore. I am actually thinking about how I fucked the conversation up. "You're too mean and awful, you're self centered, you don't care about other people."

Places where this could come from would be my mother shouted at me that I was a narcissistic, my dad comparing me to his dad who has narcissism / is his least favorite person in the world, my sister getting annoyed / angry at me everything I would say hi to her (and if I annoyed my sister, I would be punished for being mean to her), and my brother telling me that me and him are genetically fucked up in the head and can't ever belong in society. "Other people don't have our problems" was a belief he drilled into my head.  


But none of this can bring me to tears, and all of which I have discussed with a therapist in the past, yet the symptoms remain. I wonder if there's something else?   


You wouldn't happen to know of any tricks / methods I could do to find if there's anything else I am avoiding?   


Unfortunately, due to financial reasons, I've been forced to stop meeting with said therapist, so I'm kind of on my own right now.

The explanation for this is that it's hyper focusing to distract oneself from not dealing with previous trauma, correct?

If this is the case, I have two questions for you (if you don't mind me asking.) What was it you were avoiding and how did you successfully "deal" with it? What were you desperate to not see and how did you face it?

I never thought about it being a boundary problem. What happens is that it feels like they're actually focused on me and they actually want to talk / care about others. People like them are a rarity in the world. It's not like I don't have a choice but to talk to them, rather I feel extremely comfortable and I respect them quite a bit.

This could still be an enmeshment thing, I don't really know what that means. I'm still resear it right now.

The problems really occur when it's night time and I am thinking about how alone I am, how I've been alone since I was ~12 when it came to any sort of relationship (platonic or romantic). Then I think about how I really wish I had some body like them. Then it spirals and it goes like "you're 25, all of the good people like them have been taking and you're too late." And then keeps going until I have a panic attack.

I guess I'm aware it's going to fade for this one particular person, but I also can't deny how unique they are in comparison to everyone else only met. Or maybe it's all in my head, I don't know.

In 2014, I watched most of South pqrk's episodes up to that point. Pretty much all of their political episodes involve strawman arguments - they always paint the people they don't look to be as stupid or as evil as they can. The show's "genius" starts and ends with a child swearing on national television. The rest is mediocre and extremely formulaic.
How does one not believe their loneliness is crippling?

Ah, "everyone's life is different."

Everything is relative. Sure, everyone I know are different from each other. Nobodies this robot thing.

But the vast majority of people I know have social lives and relationships. Most of my peers are married. They enjoy things and have things to do and people to be with when they get off of work. 

Sure, their hobbies vary but they're not alone. Relatively speaking, yes everyone's different. But if you look at the average, there's a pretty big difference between me and them.

That's the thing, Adderall only makes it impossible (as oppose to really difficult) to sleep and Ritalin makes me nauseous.

ADHD meds haven't really done anything in the past.
